newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North sees improved profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North sees improved profit growth.

text.p: Minerals, forestry products and mining equipment group North Ltd said on Thursday it expected improved profit growth in coming years, underpinned by the coming onstream of new projects.
"North expects improved profit growth over the coming years as new projects, including Alumbrera, come onstream," North said in its annual report.
North predicted continued strength in the market for uranium based on increased demand reducing world inventory levels.

North said its 68.4 percent-owned Energy Resources of Australia Ltd would expand its mill to increase production capacity to 5,000 tonnes of uranium oxide by 1997/98 to take advantage of expected higher prices.
The iron ore market was expected to remain flat but zinc prices were seen improving in 1997.
"However, sales to Japan (from 65 percent-owned Robe River division) are expected to increase following the recovery of the japanese steel sector," the company added.
Sales to the United States would fall on stock reductions at Robe's major customer, Bethlehem Steel Corp, while South Korean sales were seen steady.
North's copper price outlook was for continued weakness for the next two to three years.
North said hedging would protect 76 percent of copper sales in 1996/97, 46 percent in 1997/98 and 26 percent in 1998/99 at average minimum prices between A$1.41 and A$1.45 a pound.

Gold profits were forecast to fall in the short term as grades declined at North's one third-owned Peak Hill mine, which established production records in fiscal 1995/96, and mill throughput was restricted at Kanowna Belle Gold Mines.
North said it would concentrate its capital expenditure efforts on furthering the development of the 50 percent-owned Kanowna over the next 12 months.
Customer confidence was expected to increase in the forestry market on the back of the Federal Government's decision in January to ease woodchip export licensing regulations, the company said.
North announced earlier this month a consolidated net profit for the year to June 30 of A$111.9 million, down from A$116.4 million a year earlier.
At 0400 GMT (2.00 p.m.), North shares were up 10 cents to A$3.52.
